text:
jen: FYI — Dedicated canary showing a p95 latency dive starting ~22:10 UTC after merge abcdef2. High customer risk, thinking hold rollout.
kevin: Seen it. Dashboard shows spike on model-v2-quant at ~22:09, same time as the merge.
maya: I pulled the flamegraph from the canary node: kernel_select() is oscillating between fused-attn and fallback kernels every few requests.
jen: That matches what I saw in traces — long tail where kernel selection toggles, causing microbatch splitting and cache churn.
dmitri: Any CI perf alerts?
release-bot: CI perf check failed on staging-loadtest: p95 increased 38% vs baseline (job id: perf-2312).
kevin: Repro locally on a dedicated-like profile when we enable "adaptive_prefetch_threshold" flag; turning it off restores stable kernel choice and drops p95.
maya: Profiling snippet: ```
# hot path sample
0x7f2 kernel_selector.cpp:142 select_kernel_for_batch
0x7f2 microbatch_splitter.cpp:78 split_if_needed (threshold=512->128)
0x7f2 kv_cache_manager.cpp:221 evict_prefix_entries
```
tim: So the split threshold is being lowered by the new heuristic, microbatches go from ~256->4, KV cache thrash increases, and fused-attn kernel can't warm KV caches, forced fallback.
jen: Customers on Dedicated A (SLA p95 200ms) saw brief regressions to 420ms. Support has two customers already pinged.
dmitri: Can we hotfix by pinning kernel preference or disabling the adaptive prefetch flag in canary config?
kevin: Quick rollback plan: 1) hold rollout globally, 2) revert the merge or flip the flag in the autoscaler config, 3) run perf smoke on dedicated staging with long-seq workload.
maya: Bisect plan if revert not ideal: narrow down to kernel selector commit range -> test combos of prefetch_threshold and autobatch heuristics. I can script targeted perf runs.
jen: For now I've set rollout state to "hold" and pinged oncall to prepare a revert if needed.
oncall: Acknowledged. I'm ready to apply emergency config flip.
release-bot: Rollout state set to HOLD by jen at 22:34 UTC.
kevin: Heads-up: doing flag flip in canary now (disable adaptive_prefetch_threshold). Will post results in ~5m.
maya: Also start collecting KV miss rate before/after: `redis_kv_miss_rate` + `kv_cache_evictions/sec`.
kevin: After flip: canary p95 back to baseline within 3 min. KV eviction rate dropped from 120/s -> 8/s.
jen: Great. Still need root cause: the heuristic mis-predicts microbatch size when sequence-length distribution has bimodal peaks (short+very-long). It tries to aggressively split which ruins kernel stability.
dmitri: Agree. Let's schedule follow-up: separate PR to make prefetch threshold respect seq-variance and prefer stable kernel affinity for Dedicated. Also add CI perf test with bimodal seq distribution.
jen: Filing a follow-up ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml for heuristic tuning. If anyone has immediate customers impacted, ping me and I'll escalate. :exclamation: :raised_hands: 
kevin: Adding canary logs and perf traces to the ticket (links in thread).
maya: I posted a minimal repro script in #eng-runtime-dev with instructions to reproduce on local dedicated dev cluster.
jen: Closing loop — rollout remains HOLD until PR lands and perf gate passes. Thanks all.
